root_cause: The datepicker's keydown handler only hides the calendar when the entered date is considered valid; when the date is outside the allowed min/max range, the handler does not trigger hide, leaving the picker open when focus leaves via Tab.
repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls the datepicker's hide method, ensuring the calendar closes whenever the input loses focus regardless of date validity.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker will close, preventing focus trap and preserving logical tab order.
functional_risks: Possible unintended hiding if other code expects the datepicker to remain open after blur (e.g., manual interaction after blur). However hide() is a no-op for inline pickers and safe to call multiple times, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: Typing a valid date (within min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker and moves focus to the next field.
Typing an invalid date (outside min/max) and pressing Tab closes the datepicker and moves focus to the next field.
Clicking outside the input field closes the datepicker.
Selecting a date via the calendar grid still behaves as configured (e.g., autohide).
